prompt:
I need the front end for Clipthread. A family messaging app built around sharing news stories, where every conversation is attached to the article someone sent, so relatives can talk over local and world news with each other at their own pace.

Who's using it: Nadia Haddad, 41, a nurse in Columbus who keeps up with news for her widowed mother, Samira, 72, still living in the family home in Dearborn, and her younger brother Karim in Phoenix. Samira reads the local paper closely but types slowly and often answers with voice messages.

What they're doing right now: Saturday morning Samira forwarded a Dearborn Press & Guide article about a proposed rezoning on her street that would allow four-story apartment buildings, and she sent a voice note asking whether she should go to the public hearing on Dec 1 and whether this means she ought to sell the house. Karim replied with a link to an opinion column. It's Monday evening and Nadia, between shifts, is catching up on what both of them said, finding the earlier article Samira sent in October about the same project, and replying in a way her mother can hear and understand, and maybe setting up a call with all three of them for Wednesday.

What's in the system at this point: Family group 'Haddads' with 3 members, plus a private conversation between Nadia and Karim. 58 shared articles since August, each with headline, outlet, date, the sender, and its own conversation (e.g., 'Council to weigh Warren Ave rezoning – Dearborn Press & Guide, Nov 14' has 6 messages). Messages include text, 3 voice notes from Samira (0:48, 1:12 and 0:35, each with an automatic transcript), and reactions. The related October article: 'Developer pitches mixed-use plan near Warren Ave' (Oct 9), with 4 messages. Unread for Nadia: 5 messages across 2 articles. Who has seen what (Samira has played Karim's link but not opened it). Members' time zones: Eastern for Nadia and Samira, Mountain Standard (Arizona) for Karim. Samira's preference: larger text and voice replies.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
